description:
What the code does:

Every integration test file in pkix-chain/tests/ that reads fixtures from disk (8 files: hostname_corpus.rs, mailbox_corpus.rs, verify_code_signer.rs, verify_ocsp_responder.rs, verify_smime.rs, verify_time_stamper.rs, verify_tls_client.rs, verify_tls_server.rs) defines its own byte-identical copy of:

    fn load_fixture(name: &str) -> Certificate {
        let path = std::path::PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))
            .join("tests/fixtures")
            .join(name);
        let der = std::fs::read(&path).unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("read {name}: {e}"));
        Certificate::from_der(&der).unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("parse {name}: {e}"))
    }

Verified byte-identical via md5sum across all 8 files (9470905cb8e1a8c686893f7c603f1c9a).

Additional duplication on the same root cause:
- const NOW: u64 = 1_780_272_000 in 7 of the 8 disk-reading files
- const BEFORE: u64 = 0 in 5 files
- fn anchors() -> [TrustAnchor; 1] in 3 files (hostname_corpus.rs, mailbox_corpus.rs, verify_tls_client.rs)
- A second variant fn load(der: &[u8]) -> Certificate duplicated between aia_chain_build.rs and aia_http_e2e.rs for the include_bytes! flavour

What idiomatic Rust would do:

Cargo's integration-test convention is to share helpers via tests/common/mod.rs imported from each integration test file via mod common; use common::*;. The Rust book documents this pattern explicitly under 'Submodules in Integration Tests' precisely because integration tests are separate compilation units that cannot otherwise share code.

Why it matters:

Any change to fixture loading — switching to pkix_truststore::from_der to keep the Tier-1 path through every cert ingestion in the workspace, adding a size cap, changing the fixtures directory layout for the PKIX-jbvb crate-split staging, improving error messages, or adapting to a future no-std fixture format — requires editing 8 files in lock-step. That is a maintenance hazard and a recurring source of merge-conflict friction between concurrent test additions. A reviewer reading the test directory should not have to grep 8 files to determine whether all callers of the helper are using the same shape.

A serious Rust practitioner would wince at 8 byte-identical copies of the same 7-line helper. clippy does not flag this (cross-file duplication is outside its scope), but Rust convention treats it as obvious style debt.

Scope:

Test-only — no production behaviour change, no API surface change. The fix is mechanical:

1. Create pkix-chain/tests/common/mod.rs exposing pub fn load_fixture, pub fn load (byte-form), pub fn anchors, pub const NOW, pub const BEFORE.
2. Add mod common; and use common::*; to each test file.
3. Drop the local copies.

The workspace currently has no tests/common/mod.rs anywhere, so this is introducing a new convention. The downside is minor: one extra file per crate that adopts it. The upside is concentrated maintenance for any future fixture-loading refactor and a template downstream test files in pkix-revocation, pkix-truststore, and other crates can follow when they accrete similar duplication.

Not in scope of this finding:

- aia_chain_build.rs / aia_http_e2e.rs both use fn load(der: &[u8]) over include_bytes! — that variant exists for a good reason (small AIA fixtures embed cheaply) and consolidation into the common module should preserve both shapes side by side.
- gen.py is Python and out of scope for any Rust idiom finding.

References:
- pkix-chain/tests/hostname_corpus.rs:20-26
- pkix-chain/tests/mailbox_corpus.rs:30-36
- pkix-chain/tests/verify_code_signer.rs:16-22
- pkix-chain/tests/verify_ocsp_responder.rs:28-34
- pkix-chain/tests/verify_smime.rs:23-29
- pkix-chain/tests/verify_time_stamper.rs:20-26
- pkix-chain/tests/verify_tls_client.rs:28-34
- pkix-chain/tests/verify_tls_server.rs:22-28
- pkix-chain/tests/aia_chain_build.rs:38-40 (byte-form sibling)

title: pkix-chain tests: load_fixture + NOW/BEFORE/anchors() duplicated across 8 test files; consolidate via tests/common/mod.rs
